First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{3}{5},\,-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{4}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{25}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{4}{5})} \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
